lots.guide_summary: Sold: 6 close plain 18ct bands at Gowans 1.2g to 2.2g made $150 to $280 hammer (about $122 to $139 per gram); the two nearest weights (1.8g, 2.0g) made $220 and $250. Unsold: a 2.1g band passed in with 8 bids (Aug 2026). Asking: scrap buyer pays about $215 for 1.7g. Melt (not a sale): spot US$4152/oz x 1.4328 AUD/USD = A$191.3/g pure, 18ct A$143.5/g, 1.7g = A$244. The earlier $600 hammer for this same ring is excluded (see dropped_entries). All AUD.
lots.working: Keep: lowest same-weight close SOLD (1.8g band, $220 hammer, Aug 2026) / 1.198 = $183.6, round down to $180 (all-in $215.64, about scrap value and under melt of $244). Flip: likely resale $220 (Gowans-type hammer for 1.7 to 2.0g bands) less 15% seller commission ($33) = $187, no postage (local pickup) = $187 / 2.396 = $78, round down to $75. The flip margin is thin, so only worth it as a keep. Buyer's premium 19.8%, inbound freight $0.
lots.confidence_reason: Marks read clearly (S+H, 18CT, D) and several opened Gowans SOLD comparables, but the stamp is a maker's carat stamp, not an assay mark (Gowans has sold 'marked 18ct, tests 15ct' rings), weight not checkable, and the earlier $600 result for this same ring is unexplained.
lots.dropped_entries: Dropped Gowans lot 437061 ($600 hammer, listed 2026-09-13) as a SOLD comparable: I compared its photos with this lot and it is the same physical ring (identical S+H / 18CT / D stamps, same spacing and wear), re-offered four weeks later. The $600 most likely did not complete (buyer default) or was an outlier, so it cannot set a value; treat it as a warning only. Dropped Lawsons lot 301 ($325) and Lawsons lot 304 ($300): snippet only, Lawsons pages return 202/403 to curl and WebFetch so not verified, weights unknown, and the W Kerr band is an antique maker piece. No mislabelled kinds otherwise; added unsold lot 433736 and sold lot 412874 that the researcher missed.
lots.key_photo_findings: Photo 2 (enlarged): S+H maker mark, 18CT, and a D in a rounded cartouche, crisp. Photo 1: plain half-round band, even wear, no dents or splits seen. Side-by-side with Gowans past lot 437061 photos shows the identical ring.
lots.condition: Light wear, no damage seen. Weight and carat not verifiable from photos.
lots.question_for_gowans: Is this the same ring as lot 437061 that hammered at $600 on the 13 September listing, and did that sale fall through? Has the ring been acid or XRF tested as 18ct (it has a maker's 18CT stamp but no assay office mark), and is 1.7g the checked weight?

lots.working: No single SOLD entry is the same pair, so the keep figure uses the lowest opened same-kind damaged SOLD rate: $120 / 2.9g = $41.4/g (lot 438571, Sept 2026; lot 440125 is $41.7/g). 7.4g x $41.4 = $306 equivalent / 1.198 = $255.6, round down to $255; I cap it at $250 for the unknown damage and pin metal (all-in $299.50, below the scrap offer of about $317 to $380). Flip: likely resale $306 hammer (same per-gram rate) less 15% seller commission ($46) = $260, no postage (local) = $260 / 2.396 = $108, round down to $105. Buyer's premium 19.8%, inbound freight $0.
lots.confidence_reason: Marks only partly legible (bar brooch 9/375 type stamp, Mother brooch British hallmark set not fully read), damage unspecified, gold weight net of pins and stones unknown, and the bid limit rests on per-gram scaling of other brooches rather than a same-item sale.
lots.dropped_entries: Dropped the eBay AU $179 'Edwardian double bar brooch' entry: snippet only, no URL, eBay closed to us, and an eBay price shown in a snippet cannot be confirmed as sold or asking. Removed the metalcharts 9K melt figure from ASKING: melt is a floor, not an asking price; the page opened today shows US$50.02/g (researcher had US$49.88 from a snippet), now used in the working only. Researcher's assumed rates (1 GBP = 2.0, 1 USD = 1.54 AUD) replaced with checked rates (1 USD = 1.4328 AUD, 1 GBP = 1.898 AUD). Badgers entry kept as SOLD category guide but it is over 24 months old.
lots.key_photo_findings: Photo 1: bar brooch looks intact (stone and both pearl trefoils present); Mother brooch has several empty pearl settings and a slightly bent tail. Photo 2 (enlarged): bar brooch reverse stamped with a 9-type numeral, a round mark and 375-type digits, worn. Photo 3 (enlarged): Mother brooch reverse has three cartouches, consistent with a British 9ct hallmark (town mark looks like an anchor, Birmingham), and the pin hinge looks grey, possibly base metal.
lots.condition: Damaged as described: Mother brooch missing several seed pearls and possibly bent; bar brooch appears largely intact. Pins may not be gold.
lots.question_for_gowans: What is the damage on each brooch, and how many pearls are missing? Are the pins gold or base metal, and what is the gold weight without them? Has the red stone been checked (garnet or glass)?
